To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have designed, synthesized, and tested pH-responsive artemisinins that are incorporated into nanoparticles and are capable of inducing apoptosis in breast cancer cells by down-regulating HER family members and cyclin D.
we have developed a pH-responsive artemisin dimers and liposomal nanoparticles that can inhibit the growth of HER+ breast cancer cells.
we have synthesized a new pH-sensitive artemisinin derivative that can be incorporated into liposomal nanoparticles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of pH-responsive artemisinins for liposomal nanoparticulate formulations.
the design, synthesis, and characterization of novel pH-responsive ART dimers and their lipid nanoparticles for the treatment of breast cancer cells in vitro.
the design, synthesis, and characterization of novel artemisinin derivatives and liposomal nanoparticles for the treatment of breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pH-sensitive ADPs and their liposomal formulations have the potential to be developed into effective therapeutics for breast cancer.
ADP Np formulations have a significant effect on the expression of HER family members in vitro.
the new pH-responsive artemisinins, ADP, when incorporated into lipid nanoparticles, are promising anti-cancer agents for the treatment of breast cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a novel artemisinin dither derivative, ADP, that is pH-responsive, is capable of being formulated in lipid NPs, and can down regulate HER family members in breast cancer cells.
we synthesized new pH-responsive ADPs and formulated them into NPs that down-regulated the oncogenic HER family members in breast cancer cells.
the new artemisinins and their liposomal nanoparticle formulation have the potential to be developed for breast cancer treatment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ADP NPS can down-regulate HER family members and survivin, and that these effects are achieved at concentrations below 1 µg/mL.
pH-responsive ADP NPs have the potential to inhibit the growth of HER2+ breast cancer cell lines by down regulating HER2 and HER3, and to inhibit growth of TNBC cell lines by down-regulating HER1.
pH-responsive ADPs incorporated into NPs are promising candidates for further investigation in breast cancer treatment.
